howIOperate.title: Your involvement is one meeting a month.
howIOperate.body: Requirements, architecture decisions, and backlog live in the repository, as one source of truth you can read without me in the room. Every deploy pushes release notes — technical and business — to you automatically. You get proactive, high-signal updates instead of status calls, and you own the code and the pipeline from the first day, not from the last one.
howIOperate.marker1: Async-first, remote, GMT-3 — overlapping business hours with the Americas and half of Europe.
howIOperate.marker2: One scheduled meeting a month. Anything urgent has a channel; nothing urgent needs a calendar invite.
howIOperate.marker3: Decisions written down where the code is, so the next person — including future you — can reconstruct why.
howIOperate.marker4: For {years} years now, the commit log across all {repos} repositories shows one human name: mine. The only other author in it is an AI agent I built the harness for. That is what the machine buys you.

Blog.disclaimerTitle: A few honest warnings before you leave

disclaimer.heading: A few honest warnings before you leave:
disclaimer.language: On the language: English is not my native language. I Speak Brazilian Portuguese, Baianese, Mineirese and a lot of bulshit. I write in it anyway — partly for reach, partly as practice. If something reads strangely, that's YOU! Your fault! You are the English Specialist, not me. I am the guy who lost the kidney of his mother-in-law!
disclaimer.ai: On AI: Yes, I use AI to help me write — the same way I use an IDE to write code, a calculator to avoid embarrassing arithmetic, and Google to remember things I definitely learned and totally didn't immediately forget. AI is a tool. I'm the one choosing what to say; the machine just helps me say it less incomprehensibly.
disclaimer.opinions: On the opinions: I'm a programmer, not a writer, journalist, analyst, or prophet. These are my personal thoughts — informal, fallible, and entirely unscientific. They exist for my own clarity, for the mild amusement of anyone who stumbles here, and for the future embarrassment of my descendants. If you disagree, you're probably right. If you agree, I appreciate your questionable judgment.

timeline.text: Went from hobbyist to professional developer.
Diagnosed with Chronic Kidney Disease. Lost both kidneys, started hemodialysis.
Family decided on a kidney transplant. My mother-in-law donated hers.
Received the transplant — a new lease on life.
Health forced a full stop from work to focus on treatment.

About.timelineClosing: I stand strong, having only lost three kidneys and broken two legs.
